headline: A real component with a full pseudo-state matrix and a 992px flip rewards resolving that matrix during the build: the four compile-time lanes all finish above hand-written vanilla, and next-yak's own no-fold lane costs 2.06×.

microbench.why: The DenseButton carries `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:active`, `:disabled`, a 992px responsive flip and a `::before` target-size rule, so there is a genuine state matrix to resolve. `next-yak-css` at 936,000 renders/s and `next-yak` at 928,000 lead because that matrix compiles to static rules and the element receives a literal class; `stylex-layers` at 912,000 sits in the same band with its atomic classes precomputed. All three finish above hand-written `vanilla` at 822,000, which still calls a component per instance. `next-yak-nofold` at 450,000 is that same source unfolded, so folding is worth 2.06× on this one component, while `emotion` at 147,000 and `panda-props` at 110,000 rebuild the matrix for every button.

autocannon.why: `next-yak-css` at 639 req/s and `next-yak` at 633 lead `vanilla` at 553, and `next-yak-nofold` at 344 prices the same component unfolded. `panda-props` at 84 req/s is the floor, more than seven times behind the leaders, because each style prop is resolved inside the request.

attribution.why: `next-yak` totals 1.35 ms with 0.292 ms of lib self-time, while `next-yak-css` and `stylex-layers` both reach 0.000 ms of lib time for a 1.39 ms total. `next-yak-nofold` needs 2.49 ms, 1.23 ms of it the wrapper. The runtime lanes carry the state matrix into render itself: 5.46 ms for `styled-components`, 7.40 ms for `emotion`, and 9.83 ms for `panda-props` with the work booked against the component.

hydrate.why: Seven lanes hydrate between 56.5 ms and 58.5 ms, because the state matrix already sits in the sheet and hydration only has to match markup. `styled-components` and `goober` both need 155 ms, since they rebuild that matrix in the client before React can attach.

inp.why: Six lanes answer a state change between 6.9 ms and 7.1 ms. The far end separates for a reason that matters: `next-yak-nofold` at 11.7 ms, `styled-components` at 15.2 ms, `panda-props` at 25.5 ms and `emotion` at 28.0 ms all re-derive the state matrix at the moment the button changes state, which is the moment a user is looking at it.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Seven lanes mount between 105 ms and 108 ms. `next-yak-nofold` at 118 ms and the runtime lanes from 148 ms to 176 ms carry their per-instance work into the mount, where it adds to parse and layout rather than replacing them.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, 0.351 ms to 0.513 ms, the widest band in the suite because this component's sheet gives the engine the most selectors to match. The ordering still does not follow render speed.

payload.why: The state matrix costs roughly the same in CSS however it is authored: `next-yak-css` ships 4,303 gz B, `vanilla` 4,444 B, `next-yak` 4,969 B. What differs is JS — 346 B for the css prop, 1,152 B for the styled runtime, 13.0 kB for `emotion` and 13.5 kB for `styled-components`. `cnfast` totals 22.3 kB, the largest here, combining an 11.6 kB merge runtime with class lists in the markup.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

nsweep.why: Five lanes hold between 4.36 ms and 4.68 ms at the largest size. `next-yak-nofold` at 9.92 ms is 2.28× its folded sibling, and `panda-props` at 39.0 ms is nearly nine times the leaders, because every state in the matrix is recomputed per instance and the count multiplies it.
